subject: Safeguard Pack — structure, escalations, and committed pricing
messages:
From: Samira Javed <samira.j@Nimbus-Analytics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick: premium SLA options and ballpark economics

Hi Alex / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the performance looked promising. We need to bake a premium support option into our procurement packet that covers a global production service (customer-facing analytics) and would be comfortable for finance and security to approve. High level asks:
- Uptime guarantees and how credits are applied for different bands
- Response times for sev1 / sev2 (including on-call escalation path)
- Cost for 12- and 24-month committed spends (we're evaluating both) and any early-payment discounts
- What extra you include for regional failover and runbooks / runbook handoff

Could you send a concise package (tiers + pricing + what’s required from our side) by early next week? Procurement is aiming for a 11/12 LOE decision.

Thanks —
Samira
Samira Javed
Head of Platform Engineering | Nimbus Analytics

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samira Javed <samira.j@Nimbus-Analytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: premium SLA options and ballpark economics

Hi Samira —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a one-pager (SLA_Safeguard_Pricing_v1.pdf) and a simple commit exhibit (redwood-commit-exhibit.xlsx) — summary below. TL;DR: we can structure three bands with clear credits and an optional 24/7 engineering retainer for Gold.

SLA Safeguard — summary (high level)
- Bronze — 99.9% monthly uptime; Sev1 response 4 hours; credit = 5% monthly invoice for <SLA threshold; no on-call retainer.
- Silver — 99.95% monthly uptime; Sev1 response 1 hour; credit = 10% monthly invoice; includes automated failover playbook and quarterly playbook review.
- Gold — 99.99% monthly uptime; Sev1 response 30 minutes (option to 15 minutes with on-call retainer); credit = 20% monthly invoice; includes 24/7 engineering escalation + regional failover runbook + two tabletop DR exercises per year.

Pricing notes (ballpark)
- Base uplift (no commit): Bronze +8% on hosted usage, Silver +18%, Gold +35%.
- 12-month commit: additional 7% off the uplift.
- 24-month commit (prepaid): additional 12% off the uplift and a small implementation credit (one-time).
- On-call retainer (Gold): $22,500 / month for guaranteed 15-minute pager escalation handled by a named Redwood engineering lead (or $12,000 / month for 30-minute escalation).

We’ll need: expected monthly token volume, regions in scope, and whether you want the 24/7 retainer to be multi-region. If you can share target spend range we’ll return a calibrated quote.

Next steps: I can loop Marissa (ops) to confirm runbook handoff and deliverable schedule, and Vanessa to finalize commercial terms. Would you like a formal quote / SOW to route to procurement?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Samira Javed <samira.j@Nimbus-Analytics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Olson <tim.olson@Nimbus-Analytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: premium SLA options and ballpark economics

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications before we pull together numbers:
1) For Gold, if we do the 24-month prepaid commit, can you reduce the on-call retainer cost (we'd expect some scale discount)?
2) For credits: how are partial-month incidents accounted for across multiple regions? Our infra is split across us-west and eu-west and we want aggregated metrics not siloed credits.
3) We want the 15-minute escalation to be staffed by Redwood engineers who have runbook familiarity and an agreed pager rota — can you map how handoffs work and SLAs for knowledge transfer?

Procurement asked for two price scenarios: a conservative 12-month commit (mid-range volume) and an aggressive 24-month prepaid (higher volume). Can you push formal pricing and the SOW by COB Tuesday 11/3?

Samira
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samira Javed <samira.j@Nimbus-Analytics.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: premium SLA options and ballpark economics

Hi Samira — looping a couple of specifics and a commercial counter-proposal.

1) Commit discounts:
- 12-month commit (target mid volume): we can offer 12% off the uplift (vs. 7% indicated) if you commit to a minimum monthly usage band (outlined in the attached exhibit).
- 24-month prepaid: we can offer 20% off the uplift + a $20k implementation credit if prepaid at Q-sign (this is already aggressive; needs CFO sign-off).

2) On-call retainer pricing (Gold):
- 15-minute escalation with named Redwood on-call lead: $18,000 / month (with 24m prepaid reduces to $14,500 / month).
- 30-minute escalation option: $9,750 / month.

3) Credits & multi-region incidents:
We can support aggregated monthly uptime across specified regions (US-WEST + EU-WEST) for credit calculations provided we define the failover boundaries in the runbook and include active health checks. We'll note that in the SOW: aggregated SLA measurement, not per-region, for the two regions you listed.

4) Knowledge transfer & runbook handoff:
Marissa (ops) will own the runbook handoff. Acceptance criteria:
- two runbook walkthrough sessions with your on-call team
- one shadowed incident during a non-peak window (optional)
- final signoff by your platform lead

Next steps: I’ll prepare the SOW + formal quote and attach the DocuSign path. If you’re good with the 24m prepaid concession we can include the reduced retainer in the exhibit. Can we get an LOI by 11/10 to keep the implementation window for January?

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Javed <samira.j@Nimbus-Analytics.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: premium SLA options and ballpark economics

Samira — quick operational notes to confirm what we’ll deliver in the SOW and how escalation maps to runbook items. Forwarding so procurement has the operational picture.

Operational commitments included in SOW:
- Escalation ladder: Support -> Technical Support Lead (Redwood) -> Named Engineering Lead (Gold retainer) -> Engineering Director on-call (for SEV1 unresolved after 2 hours).
- On-call rota: Redwood will provide a named primary + backup for the retainer; we’ll publish a monthly calendar and 24h contact numbers in the runbook.
- DR & failover: we’ll ship a regional failover playbook (runbook pages) and run two tabletop exercises per year for Gold; for Silver we provide the playbook and one tabletop exercise annually.
- Measurement: aggregated monthly uptime across us-west + eu-west; minor regional transient blips (<3 minutes) are excluded if automatic failover occurred per playbook.

Commercial implication we discussed internally: adding multi-region aggregated SLA increases operational margin; that’s why the uplift for Gold is higher. If Nimbus is willing to accept a 30-day onboarding period where we validate traffic shaping and runbook hooks, we can cap the initial retainer at 75% for the first month.

Samira — I’ll attach a short runbook TOC in the SOW and a draft escalation matrix. If that sounds good I’ll ask legal to bake the aggregated-measure clause into the SLA language.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Ops | Redwood Inference
